plan.summary: Three medium stories add an inspectable retirement preview, guarded cleanup with recovery, and a bounded daily sweep. Only freshly verified closed owners qualify; local-only content and unmerged history remain protected. Existing logs explain closure checks, decisions and outcomes. No manual apply, archive tags, dashboard or new scheduler framework.

stories.title: Preview safe retirement of registered task resources

user_story.want: inspect which completed task resources can be retired and why others must stay
user_story.benefit: I can review cleanup before it removes anything, without mistaking closed work for safely preserved work
notes: Size: M. Evidence is collected during Implement; this Plan does not claim passing execution.

Evidence inventory AC-001–AC-006: unit cases and captured CLI output; real temporary bare-origin/worktree fixtures and controlled httptest GitHub responses for closure/ref/file handling. Sources: existing internal/gittest, CLI/daemon/GitHub test patterns; new cases required. Bounds: installed Git and current repository, synthetic forge handling only; no claim about hosted availability. Missing prerequisite: Implement must execute and retain these checks.

acceptance_criteria.text: The preview command litefactory task retire enumerates registered canonical resource owners, including externally closed tasks, remote-only resources and owners missing from open-issue polling. It prints deterministic exact path/ref, proposed action and reason. Shared resources use their parent owner; lf/* naming alone never proves ownership.

Only a successful individual GitHub issue response matching the expected repository/issue identity and state closed permits eligibility. Open, 404, timeout, rate limit, null, malformed, unknown or mismatched responses produce explicit keep/unknown decisions. Validation/PR merge flags and closure reason cannot replace closure or commit proof.

Worktree expiry uses the last completed run finish time, successful or failed, plus configured worktree_retain_days; no-run owners may use a valid creation timestamp only with certain ownership. Preserve the 14-day default and existing bounds. Never use lock-mutated UpdatedAt. Active/prelaunch work and checkout-dependent pending operations remain ineligible.

Fresh successful fetch/prune and a verified remote base are required. Owned expired worktrees qualify only when tracked/staged, untracked and ignored content are absent and their local tip is reachable from the fresh remote task tip or remote base. Dirty or locally unpreserved tasks defer all resource retirement; missing upstream alone proves nothing.

Each local and remote branch requires its own exact-tip ancestry into the fresh remote base. Keep unmerged or only squash/rebase/cherry-pick-equivalent history. Remote branch eligibility is independent of worktree retention; a local branch stays while any worktree uses it. Protect configured base/default branches, wrong/detached/locked paths and uncertain/manual resources.

Preview uses the shared evaluator, never deletes resources, clears ownership, records successful retirement or advances the automatic schedule. Fetch updates are allowed; results are explicitly advisory and cannot authorize later mutations. Evaluation produces structured evidence for logging, including observation time, issue state/error, retention evidence and relevant SHAs.

stories.title: Retire eligible resources with guarded deletion and recovery

user_story.want: have eligible worktrees and merged branches removed safely
user_story.benefit: finished checkouts stop consuming space while local-only work and unfinished history remain recoverable
notes: Size: M. Evidence is collected during Implement; this Plan does not claim passing execution.

Evidence inventory AC-001–AC-008: unit failure/closure/log capture and source/surface review; temporary real migrated SQLite, bare Git origin/worktrees and httptest lifecycle cases for locking, exact-head races, intent/crash windows and recreation. Sources: existing internal/gittest/store/daemon patterns; new feature tests required. Bounds: installed Git/current repository; fixture forge responses prove handling only. Record Git version and scratch probe for new external Git behavior. Missing prerequisite: execute and retain criterion-attributed checks during Implement.

acceptance_criteria.text: Only the daemon executor performs new retirement mutations. Acquire existing canonical task/managed-parent ownership before the clone gate, re-read active/prelaunch and required pending-effect state under coordination, and skip unsafe ownership. Recheck the issue through GetIssue with WithoutConditionalCache immediately before mutation; reopened or unverifiable issues cancel deletion.

Revalidate exact registered path/ref identity and fresh Git preservation before deletion; perform unforced worktree removal only after explicit tracked/staged/untracked/ignored checks. Remove qualifying worktree before its local branch. Never recursively delete guessed paths, force worktree removal, delete another worktree's branch or remove the configured base/default branch.

Independently guard each local and remote branch deletion against the previously verified exact head; a changed head rejects mutation and is reported for retry. Real Git tests demonstrate remote server-side expected-head rejection and local compare-and-delete rejection. Remote-only and already-removed-worktree owners remain supported without modifying the registered clone checkout, index or HEAD.

Persist minimal per-resource intent including owner, original path/ref, expected SHAs and intended action before each deletion. Intent write failure prohibits deletion. Confirm effects before reporting removed/clearing a worktree path; failed confirmation or outcome persistence leaves a distinguishable uncertain retryable record, never claimed success. Store transactions do not span Git/HTTP/filesystem I/O.

On retry/restart, reacquire coordination and reconcile only exact owned resources, including already absent paths/refs and stale owned worktree registrations. A retained old intent does not authorize deletion of a recreated checkout or advanced branch. Preserve session/branch identity, run reports, acceptance and delivery records throughout partial or complete cleanup.

Reopening after full or partial cleanup recreates the checkout on the next authorized run through existing EnsureWorktree behavior: surviving local branch, remote branch, then fresh remote base. Regression cases cover factory/external closure, won't-do/duplicate abandonment, open merged issue, absent upstream, shared children, active work, local-only files/commits and partial retirement.

Every initial/final closure observation and resource decision/mutation emits structured retirement logs at normal visibility: sweep/task/repository/issue, timestamp/source/phase, returned state/reason or error, path/ref, preview/apply, relevant retention/SHAs, action/reason and actual outcome. Distinguish would_remove, removed, kept, already_absent, failed and unknown. Ordinary decisions are Info, unavailable verification Warn, mutation/storage failures Error; omit credentials, bodies and file contents.

Deliberately amend the SEC-7/S-6 exact Git capability contract, package comments and surface tests only as necessary for owned task-branch maintenance and required read-only probes. Permit exact-head guarded retirement without checkout/commit/reset/pull of the registered clone; preserve clone checkout/index/HEAD and base/default protection tests. This narrow policy amendment is part of the explicitly requested branch-retirement scope.

stories.title: Run daily retirement and explain its outcomes

user_story.want: have cleanup run daily with visible results and an inspectable preview
user_story.benefit: I can rely on the retention setting and understand what was removed or deferred
notes: Size: M. Evidence is collected during Implement; this Plan does not claim passing execution.

Evidence inventory AC-001–AC-005: fake-clock/channel unit tests, captured logs/help review, temporary real SQLite/Git and controlled forge restart/lifecycle tests; aggregate make check. Sources: existing daemon/store/Git test utilities and config/help files, feature tests to be written. Bounds: repository/offline dependency behavior, not production deletion or hosted availability. Missing prerequisite: Implement execution and retained outcomes.

acceptance_criteria.text: After normal startup recovery, daemon Tick admits a due sweep and processes bounded batches using supplied daemon time, without a new scheduler goroutine or synchronous full scan every tick/startup. Daily means 24 elapsed hours after a completed pass; preserve due/progress state across restart so repeated restarts do not restart full scans.

Persist stable sweep identity, owner cursor/pass boundary and due state using minimal store state. Progress fairly through registered owners; an owner failure/deferment does not starve later owners, and deferred owners are reconsidered next pass. Respect existing GitHub request budgets/backoff, normal polling capacity, cancellation and shutdown with bounded batch contexts.

Route automatic decisions/deletions through the shared evaluator and guarded executor. Emit default-visible retirement summaries with sweep identity, duration, action/outcome counts and deferred/incomplete work, including zero-candidate passes. Interrupted or storage-failed passes are not labelled completed or advanced as successful.

Update config template, task clean help and operator documentation so worktree_retain_days truthfully describes active daily cleanup and last-completed-run retention, including no-run fallback. Explain task retire preview, existing logs --all --grep retirement, ignored-content skips, strict ancestry limitations, external closure/abandonment behavior and the residual reopen race after the final GitHub read. Preserve existing manual task clean behavior.

Executed lifecycle tests cover first due pass, 24-hour boundary, restart continuation, zero candidates, owner errors, backoff, shutdown and task/clone contention using controlled time/synchronization and temporary real store/Git dependencies where needed. Run and retain passing make check for the complete feature; never build into dist or use integration tags/names.
